title.narrative: Promoting Participatory Governance and Human Rights in DRC

description.narrative: Africa’s destiny will be shaped by how much Africa constructs a sense of belief in democracy, governance and unity as the most viable policy option to mediate, reconcile and accommodate the individual and collective interests. The current situation in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is highlighted by the change of the Article 220 of the constitution aimed to allow the current president to go for a third term. This is a substantially challenged by the Catholic church, the foreign diplomats and even members of his own ruling coalition especially now at the wake of the Blaise Compaoré's precipitous fall from power in Burkina Faso, the lid has been put on this campaign of constitution change. Now the president and his ruling party have changed the strategy and might chose to sidestep controversy and simply delay the holding of presidential elections by introducing a national census that may go until 2020. The current DRC political situation is volatile as the general population has become more upset of the economic situation. Moreover, many are not well educated on the issues related to constitutional change as well as resource allocation and management. The general population also has limited analytical capacities to read behind the current political intentions. The Catholic Church has been doing it best to educate the population by producing leaflets in various local languages. However, this has not been sufficient due to the size of the country and the changing political situation. Ahead of the local and presidential election, this project aims to support Church structures at national and international level to carry out advocacy initiatives on issues related to Constitutional review; to support local organizations to monitor the public spending based on voted budget, and to strengthen the security of church leaders and local organizations engaged in human rights activities. The project will be run for six months, and will be implemented by the CEJP in partnership with RENADHOC and CADICEC. The expected results are: - The bishops Episcopal Conferences of DRC and the ACEAC in the region (Congo Brazzaville) will advocate at the regional level against the risks of change of constitution and the benefits of alternation of power; - The Civil Society Organizations will improve their skills to engage in public budget monitoring; - The churches and CSOs leaders will be engaged in the promotion of fundamental human rights and human right defenders will improve their security management skills.
